raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  name: verilator
  version: "5.052"
  sha256: 8c8d2e11e6ad32f641dd250742a94195ddecb912e2e2dabe2f42ddbbb99c1092

recipe:
  name: verilator-packages
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/${{ name }}/${{ name }}/archive/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: ${{ sha256 }}
  patches:
    - patches/0004-add-message-suggesting-verilator-debug-package.patch
    - patches/0005-cross-compile-cxx14-detection.patch

build:
  number: 0

outputs:
  - staging:
      name: verilator-build
    build:
      script:
        file: build
        env:
          CONDA_BUILD_CROSS_COMPILATION: ${{ "1" if build_platform != target_platform else "0" }}
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - distro
        - perl
        - python
        - git  # for patching
        - if: not win
          then:
            - autoconf
            - bison
            - help2man
            - make
            - sed
          else:
            - cmake
            - winflexbison
      host:
        - zlib
        - if: not win
          then: flex  # need to link against it for target

  - package:
      name: verilator
    inherit: verilator-build
    build:
      script: install
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - if: win
          then: cmake
          else:
            - make
            - ripgrep
            - perl
      host:
        - zlib
        - if: not win
          then: flex  # need to link against it for target
      run:
        - perl
        - python
        - if: osx
          then:
            - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
            - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        # there must be a way to derive this from compiler('cxx') but this should work
        - if: linux and x86_64
          then: gxx_impl_linux-64
        - if: not win
          then:
            - ${{ pin_compatible('flex') }}
            - make
    tests:
      - requirements:
          run:
            - cmake
            - python >=3
            - if: not win
              then:
                - pkgconfig
                - make
                - graphviz
                # only need C compiler because cmake bails if it doesn't have one.
                # at least with the CMakeLists.txt in the examples
                - ${{ compiler('c') }}
                # re-install the default compiler package with activation scripts
                # because it is the easiest way to get cmake to work in the sanity checks
                # for cmake.  However, normal makefile based tests do not need this and
                # will work fine because verilated.mk builds in the path to the c++ compiler
                - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        script:
          - if: win
            then: where verilator
            else: pkg-config --print-provides verilator
          - verilator --version
          - if: not win
            then: cp -r "$PREFIX"/share/verilator/examples .
          - if: linux
            then: for d in examples/*; do echo $d; make -C $d; done
          - if: osx
            then: for d in examples/make*; do echo $d; make -C $d; done

  - package:
      name: verilator-debug
    inherit: verilator-build
    build:
      script: install
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
      run:
        # depending on the verilator package here breaks testing the package because
        # the solver can't install the verilator package yet
        # - ${{ pin_subpackage('verilator', exact=True) }}
    tests:
      - script:
          - if: win
            then: where verilator_bin_dbg
          - verilator_bin_dbg --version

about:
  license: LGPL-3.0-only OR Artistic-2.0
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - LICENSES/Artistic-2.0.txt
  summary: The fastest Verilog HDL simulator
  description: |
    Welcome to Verilator, the fastest Verilog HDL simulator.
      • Accepts synthesizable Verilog or SystemVerilog
      • Performs lint code-quality checks
      • Compiles into multithreaded C++, or SystemC
      • Creates XML to front-end your own tools
    Fast
      • Outperforms many commercial simulators
      • Single- and multi-threaded output models
    Widely Used
      • Wide industry and academic deployment
      • Out-of-the-box support from Arm, and RISC-V vendor IP
    Community Driven & Openly Licensed
      • Guided by the CHIPS Alliance and Linux Foundation
      • Open, and free as in both speech and beer
      • More simulation for your verification budget
    Commercial Support Available
      • Commercial support contracts
      • Design support contracts
      • Enhancement contracts
  homepage: https://veripool.org/wiki/verilator
  documentation: https://www.veripool.org/projects/verilator/wiki/Documentation
  repository: https://github.com/verilator/verilator

    - timkpaine
    - timsnyder
